description: h^max estimates the cost from a state to the goal of a planning task. It uses the *delete relaxation*: a fact that becomes true stays true, so operators never undo each other. The cost of a fact is the cost of the cheapest operator that adds it, plus the cost of that operator's most expensive precondition; the estimate is the cost of the most expensive goal fact. h^max never overestimates (it is *admissible*), so A* with it finds cheapest plans, but its estimates are often low. Decoupled search keeps a *price* (cheapest cost) for each reached leaf state; there, each fact starts at the cheapest price of a reached leaf state that contains it.

papers.title: Beating LM-Cut with h^max (Sometimes): Fork-Decoupled State Space Search
papers.venue: International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS)
